# Backlog tasks and plan specs

    10|This repo uses a **two-tier** pattern for some work. Most tasks are Backlog-only; initiative-scale agent work may also have plan specs under `plan/<initiative>/`.

## Roles

| Layer | Location | Holds |
|-------|----------|-------|
| **Ticket** | `backlog/tasks/` (via CLI) | Status, deps, AC, assignee, `--plan` / `--notes` / `--final-summary` |
| **Runbook** | `plan/<initiative>/tasks/` (optional) | Stable execution steps, deliverables, result history |

Backlog owns **commitment** (what, why, when done). Plan specs own **procedure** (how to run it) when the how is known upfront and agent-oriented.
    20|
## When to add a plan spec

Add a linked plan spec file when work is:

- Initiative-scale and spans sessions or handoffs
- Agent-executed with procedural steps (prompt pipelines, multi-repo orchestration)
- Backed by shared assets in `plan/<initiative>/` (`background/`, `prompts/`, etc.)

Use **Backlog only** for typical toolkit work (scripts, analyzers, bug fixes, refactors). Research the approach at pickup; record `--plan` on the backlog task — do not pre-write a side spec.

# Weather forecast discrepancy: Open-Meteo vs Google Weather

    10|## Context

The TRMNL dashboard fetches weather forecasts from the free [Open-Meteo API](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs). A user observed that the dashboard often looks gloomier than Google Weather, predicting rain on days when Google does not.

## Investigation (2026-07-23)

### Location and method

- Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (default config: `WEATHER_LATITUDE=52.3676`, `WEATHER_LONGITUDE=4.9041`).
- Open-Meteo request: same parameters used by `src/weather.py` (`daily=weather_code,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,precipitation_probability_max`, `forecast_days=5`).
    20|- Comparison source: [AccuWeather 10-day forecast for Amsterdam](https://www.accuweather.com/en/nl/amsterdam/249758/daily-weather-forecast/249758). AccuWeather is a reasonable proxy for the consumer-grade forecast Google Weather presents in its UI.

Raw data and scripts are stored alongside this document in `backlog/docs/weather/`.

### Side-by-side forecast

| Date | Open-Meteo daily code | Open-Meteo description | Precip sum | Max PoP | AccuWeather description | AccuWeather PoP | Match? |
|------|----------------------|------------------------|------------|---------|-------------------------|-----------------|--------|
| 2026-07-23 | 51 | Light drizzle | 0.2 mm | 4% | Rather cloudy | 7% | **No** |
| 2026-07-24 | 51 | Light drizzle | 0.1 mm | 10% | Pleasant with a sun-and-cloud mix | 25% | **No** |
    30|| 2026-07-25 | 3 | Overcast | 0.0 mm | 12% | Mostly sunny and delightful | 4% | **No** |
... 52 lines not shown ...

  141:When asked to work on a task, run `backlog task view TASK-N --plain` first. If status is **Refinement** or **Done**, **warn the user and stop** — do not assign, plan, or implement. Only proceed for **To Do** or **In Progress**. Move a refined ticket with `backlog task edit TASK-N -s "To Do"`.
  145:"Next task" means lowest `ordinal` among **To Do** tasks (Refinement is excluded), not lowest ticket ID and not creation order. Ordinal is the manual ordering field (`backlog task list --plain` and the board reflect it) — a task created later can still sort before one created earlier if its ordinal is lower. Always resolve "next"/"the next task in the backlog" by checking ordinal, not by assuming ticket-ID or creation-date order.
  147:### Worktree split: Backlog metadata vs. implementation
  149:Backlog task lifecycle actions (`task create`, `task edit -s <status>`, `-a <assignee>`, `--plan`, `--notes`, `--final-summary`, `--check-ac`, etc.) always run from the **main worktree** — see the Backlog.md rule under Multi-agent workflow above for why (serial task IDs, git-tracked `backlog/tasks/`). The **actual implementation work** for a task (code changes, config changes, running scripts, anything beyond Backlog metadata) happens in a **per-task worktree** created with `./scripts/new_worktree.sh <branch-name>`, not in the main worktree. Typical flow: from main worktree, create/move the task to its active status and record the plan; `cd` into (or spawn an agent in) the per-task worktree to do the work; come back to the main worktree to update notes/status/final-summary and check acceptance criteria.

## Notes for agents

- `README.md` now contains the human-facing project documentation. For agent-focused details, build steps, and conventions, use this file and the files in `plan/`.
   310|- `plan/PLAN.md` is the authoritative architecture record; `plan/TASKS.md` tracks phase-by-phase progress and notes any deviations from the original plan (e.g. tasks completed earlier/later than originally scheduled, or skipped with a reason). Check both before assuming an "Open item" listed there has been resolved.
- The codebase intentionally supports running without credentials by rendering explicit error states for unconfigured sources. If you add a new data source, follow the `fetch_*_or_dummy` fallback pattern for low-level fetchers, but surface missing credentials / failures through the `errors` object in `src/unified_fetcher.py`.
- Rendering (device-specific layout, grayscale dithering) happens in `templates/*.liquid`, not in Python. If you add a new device profile in `src/config.py`, it needs a corresponding `templates/devices/<name>.liquid` template before `src/liquid_render.py`/`export_preview.py` can render it — profiles without a template (`template_filename=None`, see `STUB_PROFILE`) are valid and are skipped by both.
- This project uses Backlog.md for task management. At the start of each task-focused session, run `backlog instructions overview`. Prefer `backlog task create`, `backlog task edit`, and `backlog board` over hand-editing files in `backlog/`.

# Task statuses and agent pickup

    10|Configured board columns (`backlog/config.yml`):

| Status | Meaning | Agent may implement? |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Refinement** | Ticket exists but scope, AC, or dependencies are not final yet | **No** — warn and stop |
| **To Do** | Ready for pickup; plan is written at execution time | Yes |
| **In Progress** | Actively being worked | Yes (continue) |
| **Done** | Complete | No — terminal |

    20|

- You want a ticket ID and milestone placement before the work is agent-ready.

# Weather forecast discrepancy: Open-Meteo vs Google Weather

## Context

The TRMNL dashboard fetches weather forecasts from the free [Open-Meteo API](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs). A user observed that the dashboard often looks gloomier than Google Weather, predicting rain on days when Google does not.

## Investigation (2026-07-23)

### Location and method

- Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (default config: `WEATHER_LATITUDE=52.3676`, `WEATHER_LONGITUDE=4.9041`).
- Open-Meteo request: same parameters used by `src/weather.py` (`daily=weather_code,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,precipitation_probability_max`, `forecast_days=5`).
- Comparison source: [AccuWeather 10-day forecast for Amsterdam](https://www.accuweather.com/en/nl/amsterdam/249758/daily-weather-forecast/249758). AccuWeather is a reasonable proxy for the consumer-grade forecast Google Weather presents in its UI.

Raw data and scripts are stored alongside this document in `backlog/docs/weather/`.

### Side-by-side forecast

| Date | Open-Meteo daily code | Open-Meteo description | Precip sum | Max PoP | AccuWeather description | AccuWeather PoP | Match? |
|------|----------------------|------------------------|------------|---------|-------------------------|-----------------|--------|
| 2026-07-23 | 51 | Light drizzle | 0.2 mm | 4% | Rather cloudy | 7% | **No** |
| 2026-07-24 | 51 | Light drizzle | 0.1 mm | 10% | Pleasant with a sun-and-cloud mix | 25% | **No** |
| 2026-07-25 | 3 | Overcast | 0.0 mm | 12% | Mostly sunny and delightful | 4% | **No** |
```

# Backlog tasks and plan specs

This repo uses a **two-tier** pattern for some work. Most tasks are Backlog-only; initiative-scale agent work may also have plan specs under `plan/<initiative>/`.

## Roles

| Layer | Location | Holds |
|-------|----------|-------|
| **Ticket** | `backlog/tasks/` (via CLI) | Status, deps, AC, assignee, `--plan` / `--notes` / `--final-summary` |
| **Runbook** | `plan/<initiative>/tasks/` (optional) | Stable execution steps, deliverables, result history |

Backlog owns **commitment** (what, why, when done). Plan specs own **procedure** (how to run it) when the how is known upfront and agent-oriented.

## When to add a plan spec

Add a linked plan spec file when work is:

- Initiative-scale and spans sessions or handoffs
- Agent-executed with procedural steps (prompt pipelines, multi-repo orchestration)
- Backed by shared assets in `plan/<initiative>/` (`background/`, `prompts/`, etc.)

Use **Backlog only** for typical toolkit work (scripts, analyzers, bug fixes, refactors). Research the approach at pickup; record `--plan` on the backlog task — do not pre-write a side spec.
```
